mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above trend within 2 quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which increases wage pressures and prompts the Federal Reserve to raise rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or inflation does not rise above 3% within the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or industrial production rebounds above trend within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months signals a disinflationary tightening, which reduces real interest rates and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or inflation rises above 3% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND RSAFS > 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or either series reverts below its moving average within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the civilian unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or unemployment falls below 5% within the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or housing starts revert below trend within the next two months.
